_comment: Mobile text for area/hyrule.are, read by scripts/build_hyrule_area.py.
enemies: keyed by ENEMY_TYPES kind; every band of a kind shares it.
bosses: keyed by dungeon level; replaces the retained record's long
and description lines (and its short name, where one is given).
'long' is one line; 'description' is pre-wrapped at 75 columns.
Written from the NES game; see wiki/hyrule-area.md for the sources.

red_octorok.long: A red octorok scuttles about on stubby legs, snout puckered to spit.
red_octorok.description:
A squat, red, octopus-like creature on four stubby legs, its snout a
short tube that puckers and swells. It wanders in short, jerky bursts,
stops, turns to face its prey and spits a hard round stone. A shield
turns the stones aside. Red octoroks are slow and easily beaten.

blue_octorok.long: A blue octorok darts across the grass, spitting stones as it goes.
blue_octorok.description:
A blue, octopus-like creature on four stubby legs with a tubular
snout. Tougher and quicker than its red cousin, it zigzags about in
fast little runs, wheels to face whoever comes near and spits a hard
stone with real force. It takes several blows before it pops into a
puff of smoke.

red_moblin.long: A red moblin, a doglike brute with a spear, sniffs the air for prey.
red_moblin.description:
A hulking, doglike humanoid with a pig's snout, floppy ears and a
bristling red hide. It stalks the forest paths in a lumbering gait and
hurls crude spears at anything that crosses its line of sight. Its
hide is thick but not thick enough to turn a good sword.

blue_moblin.long: A blue moblin hefts a spear and grunts, its piggish snout twitching.
blue_moblin.description:
A big, doglike brute with a pig's snout and a blue-grey hide tougher
than any red moblin's. It patrols the deep woods in pairs and packs,
throwing spear after spear in straight lines, and it takes several
hard blows to bring down. Some of its kind keep secret caves full of
rupees and give them away, so long as nobody tells.

red_tektite.long: A red tektite crouches on long jointed legs, ready to spring.
red_tektite.description:
A one-eyed, spiderlike creature with a round red body and four long,
jointed legs. It crouches, then flings itself into the air in high,
unpredictable leaps, landing hard and springing off again before a
blade can find it. Its single eye never stops watching.

blue_tektite.long: A blue tektite bobs on its springy legs, its single eye unblinking.
blue_tektite.description:
A round blue body slung between four long, jointed legs, with one
staring eye in the middle. It leaps further and more often than the
red kind, bounding across the rocks in long arcs and dropping onto
whoever stands beneath. Catching it mid-crouch is the trick.

red_leever.long: A red leever spins up out of the sand, whirling like a drill.
red_leever.description:
A spiny, plantlike creature that lives beneath the sand and bores up
to the surface with a spinning hiss. Red leevers rise near anyone who
walks the dunes, charge straight across the ground, then dive back
under and come up somewhere else. They are weak, but they never stop.

blue_leever.long: A blue leever churns through the sand, spinning toward its prey.
blue_leever.description:
A spinning, cactus-like thing that burrows through sand and soil. The
blue kind is tougher than the red, wanders the open ground for longer
before it sinks, and turns to chase whoever it senses. Its spinning
body rasps like a millstone, and a stroke that lands must land hard.

red_lynel.long: A red lynel paws the earth, a sword in its hand and fire in its eye.
red_lynel.description:
A great four-legged beast with the body of a horse and the torso,
mane and face of a lion, armoured and carrying a heavy sword. Lynels
roam the high mountain paths and hurl blades of force from their
swords at anything in their line. Even the red ones are among the
most dangerous beasts of the overworld.

blue_lynel.long: A blue lynel stamps its hooves and levels its sword at you.
blue_lynel.description:
A centaur-like monster with a lion's head and mane, a horse's body
and blue-scaled armour over its chest. It charges the mountain
tracks and flings beams of force from its sword, and its hide shrugs
off weak blows. Blue lynels are the strongest beasts that walk the
open land of Hyrule.

peahat.long: A peahat whirls through the air on spinning petals.
peahat.description:
A great flower whose petals spin like the blades of a top, lifting it
off the ground to whirl and dip over the fields. While it spins it is
nearly impossible to hurt, and it bumps into whatever it chases. Only
when it slows and settles to rest can a blade cut it down.

zora.long: A zora surfaces in the water, its throat glowing with a fireball.
zora.description:
A finned, scaly fish-man with a wide mouth and a crest of green fins.
It hides beneath rivers and lakes, rises without warning, spits a
ball of fire at whoever stands on the bank, and sinks out of sight
before the answer can reach it. A shield can turn its fireballs.

ghini.long: A ghini drifts between the graves, its one eye fixed on the living.
ghini.description:
A pale, sheet-like ghost with a single round eye and a grinning
mouth. It floats through the graveyard passing through stone as if it
were mist, and drifts after whoever disturbs the dead. Touching a
grave can wake more of them. Strike down the first ghost of a
graveyard and the lesser ones are said to vanish with it.

armos.long: An armos statue stands motionless, spear raised, eyes of stone.
armos.description:
A stone knight with a spear and shield, carved to stand guard over
old places. Most armos statues are only stone; some wake when
touched, turn red or blue with sudden life, and march stiffly after
the one who disturbed them. Under some of them, secrets lie hidden
in the earth: a stair, a coin cache, a bracelet.

falling_rock.long: Loose boulders come bouncing down the mountainside toward you.
falling_rock.description:
Not a beast at all but the mountain itself, shedding stones. Rocks
break loose from the heights and bound down the slopes in long
high arcs, smashing anyone they land on before shattering into
gravel. They cannot be fought, only dodged or outrun, and the clatter
never stops for long.

keese.long: A keese flutters about on leathery wings, darting and pausing.
keese.description:
A small black bat with one round eye on its face. Keese roost in the
dark corners of dungeons and swarm out in jittery flights, darting,
stopping, then darting again in a new direction. A single blow kills
one, but there are always more of them than there seem to be.

gel.long: A tiny gel quivers on the floor, hopping in short bursts.
gel.description:
A small, dark blob of living jelly no bigger than a fist. Gels creep
and hop in short bursts across dungeon floors, and one that touches
you clings and slows you down. They are what is left when a zol is
cut in two, and a single stroke ends one.

zol.long: A zol, a large blob of green jelly, slides wetly toward you.
zol.description:
A big, quivering mound of green slime with two dull eyes. It slides
across the floor in sudden hops and engulfs whatever it reaches.
Strike it with a weak blade and it splits into two small gels that
keep coming; strike it hard enough and it bursts outright.

bubble.long: A bubble, a flaming skull, bounces from wall to wall.
bubble.description:
A grinning skull wreathed in flickering blue flame. It bounces around
the room in straight lines, caroming off the walls, and no weapon can
harm it. Its touch leaves a creeping numbness in the sword arm, and
those it brushes find for a while that they cannot use their blade.

rope.long: A rope slithers along the floor, its forked tongue flicking.
rope.description:
A red-and-orange snake that coils and slithers slowly about the
dungeon floor. The moment its prey lines up with it, a rope lunges in
a straight, lightning-fast charge. It is easily killed, but its bite
is sharper than its size suggests.

stalfos.long: A stalfos rattles to its feet, clutching a rusty sword.
stalfos.description:
A skeleton warrior, bones yellow with age, holding a notched sword
and sometimes a battered shield. It hops and lurches about the room in
random directions, slashing at anyone it blunders into. It falls
apart in a clatter when struck hard enough, and some carry the key
to the next locked door.

red_goriya.long: A red goriya grins, a wooden boomerang cocked to throw.
red_goriya.description:
A doglike humanoid in red armour with a long snout and pointed ears.
It paces the dungeon halls and hurls a boomerang that spins out in a
straight line and curves back to its hand, striking on the way out
and on the way home. Goriyas come in pairs and in packs.

blue_goriya.long: A blue goriya snarls and readies a heavy boomerang.
blue_goriya.description:
A doglike warrior in blue armour, stronger and more stubborn than the
red kind. Its boomerang flies farther and hits harder, and it takes
several solid blows to fell. Goriyas are fond of food, and one is said
to guard a passage in the Demon's labyrinth until it is fed.

wallmaster.long: A great hand slides out of the wall, fingers grasping.
wallmaster.description:
A huge, disembodied hand that lurks inside dungeon walls. It slides
out along the floor toward whoever stands near the edge of a room,
snatches them up, and carries them all the way back to the entrance
of the dungeon. Keep to the middle of the room and keep moving.

vire.long: A vire hops along the floor, its leathery blue wings folded.
vire.description:
A horned, blue, batlike demon with a wide grin and folded wings. It
hops across the floor in high bounds and drops onto its prey. Strike
it and it bursts apart into two red keese that flutter off to keep
the fight going. It is worth finishing the bats as well.

like_like.long: A like like squats here, a tube of flesh with a gaping mouth.
like_like.description:
A thick, tubelike mass of ribbed, pinkish flesh with a gaping mouth
at its top. It creeps slowly toward its prey and swallows whatever
it touches whole, chewing at it from inside. Anyone it engulfs is
spat out again, but often without their shield, which it eats. Kill
it quickly, or keep your distance.

pols_voice.long: A pols voice hops about, its long ears twitching at every sound.
pols_voice.description:
A round, ghostly white creature with huge rabbitlike ears and a
half-smile. It bounces about the room in long, floaty hops and is
hard to wound with a blade. It cannot stand loud noise, and an arrow
ends it at once; that is the arrow's secret power.

gibdo.long: A gibdo shuffles forward, trailing its rotting wrappings.
gibdo.description:
A mummy wrapped head to foot in yellowed, rotting linen. Gibdos
shuffle slowly but relentlessly through the tombs of the dungeons,
reaching for the living, and they take a great deal of punishment
before they fall. Fire is said to make short work of their wraps.

red_darknut.long: A red darknut advances, its great shield held squarely before it.
red_darknut.description:
A knight in full red plate armour, carrying a sword and a broad
shield. It marches about the room and always turns to face its foe,
and its shield turns aside any blow or arrow from the front. Only a
stroke from the side or from behind will bite. Red darknuts are the
lesser of their order, and still dangerous.

blue_darknut.long: A blue darknut marches toward you, shield up, sword ready.
blue_darknut.description:
A towering knight in blue plate with a heavy sword and a shield that
no blow from the front can pass. It is faster, tougher and harder
hitting than the red kind, turning to keep its shield between it and
any attacker. Get to its side or its back, or do not fight it at all.

red_wizzrobe.long: A red wizzrobe flickers into being, wand raised to cast.
red_wizzrobe.description:
A sorcerer in an orange-red robe and hood, face hidden in shadow. It
vanishes and reappears in a new spot beside or in line with its
prey, looses a beam of magic from its wand, and vanishes again. It
is only vulnerable in the moment it is visible. Strike then.

blue_wizzrobe.long: A blue wizzrobe glides through the wall, wand crackling.
blue_wizzrobe.description:
A robed and hooded sorcerer in blue, the deadlier of its kind. It
drifts about the room, flickers through solid walls, and casts beams
of magic in straight lines as it comes. It is hard to pin down and
harder to escape, and its spells strike through a shield.

red_lanmola.long: A red lanmola bursts up through the sand, its segments rippling.
red_lanmola.description:
A great centipede of armoured red segments that tunnels through sand
and loose earth. It erupts from the ground, races across the room in
a writhing line, and dives back down. Only its head can be wounded,
and each segment lost seems to make it faster.

blue_lanmola.long: A blue lanmola surges out of the sand, a blur of segments.
blue_lanmola.description:
A long, many-segmented centipede in blue armour, far faster than the
red kind. It bursts up out of the floor, streaks around the room so
quickly the eye can barely follow, and plunges back into the sand.
Only its head is soft, and it grows faster as it loses its tail.

patra.long: A patra hovers here, a great eye ringed by circling smaller eyes.
patra.description:
A giant floating eye surrounded by a ring of eight smaller eyes that
circle it endlessly, sometimes swinging out wide to strike. The
little eyes must be destroyed before the great eye can be hurt.
Patras guard the deepest halls of Death Mountain, and one of them
is said to have the map.

dodongo.long: A dodongo lumbers about, a stocky dinosaur with a thick hide.
dodongo.description:
A stout, rhinoceros-like reptile with tough grey hide and a huge
mouth. It stomps slowly back and forth, too thick-skinned for most
weapons to hurt. Set a bomb in its path and it will swallow it, and
the blast inside does what no sword can. The smoke of a bomb also
stuns it long enough to strike.

digdogger.long: A digdogger rolls about, a great spiked ball with a single eye.
digdogger.description:
A huge, spiny urchin with a single great eye at its center. It bounces
and rolls about the room, shrugging off blows from any weapon. It
hates one certain kind of sound: play the recorder, and it shrinks
and splits into smaller, faster urchins that can be struck down.

blade_trap.long: A spiked blade trap rests in the corner, waiting to slide.
blade_trap.description:
A block of spiked iron set into the corner of a dungeon room. It sits
still until something crosses its line, then shoots across the floor
at terrible speed, slams into its partner or the far wall, and grinds
slowly back to its place. It cannot be destroyed, only avoided.

1.long: Aquamentus, a horned green dragon, rears on its ledge and roars.
1.description:
A great green dragon with a single sharp horn on its head, standing
on its hind legs at the far end of the chamber. Aquamentus shuffles
back and forth along its ledge, never leaving it, and opens its jaws
to spit three fireballs at once in a spreading fan. Its scaly body
shrugs off most blows; its horned head is its only weakness. Guardian
of the Eagle, it bars the way to the first shard of wisdom, and it
leaves a heart container behind when it falls.

2.long: Dodongo, a huge triceratops-like beast, stomps toward you.
2.description:
An enormous, stocky dinosaur with a thick, armoured hide and a mouth
wide enough to swallow a man. Dodongo lumbers back and forth across
its lair, too tough for any sword. Yet it dislikes smoke: it will
swallow a bomb set in its path, and the blast inside shakes it to its
core, and the smoke of a bomb stuns it long enough for a blade to
bite. Guardian of the Moon, it leaves a heart container behind.

3.long: Manhandla, a monstrous four-headed flower, writhes toward you.
3.description:
A giant carnivorous plant with a thick central bulb and four snapping
flower heads, one on each side. Manhandla glides about the room
spitting fireballs from every mouth, and each head can be cut away on
its own. As its heads fall it grows faster and wilder, until the last
one ricochets about the chamber at frightening speed. A well-placed
bomb can take more than one head at once. Guardian of the Manji, it
leaves a heart container behind.

4.long: Gleeok, a two-headed dragon, rears and spits fire from both jaws.
4.description:
A massive dragon with two long, snakelike necks, each ending in a
horned, fire-spitting head. Gleeok stays planted against the north
wall while its necks writhe and its heads spit fireballs. Hack at a
head long enough and it tears free and flies about the room on its
own, still spitting fire. When the last head is severed, the beast
collapses. Guardian of the Snake, it leaves a heart container.

5.long: Digdogger, a giant one-eyed urchin, rolls ponderously about.
5.description:
An enormous, spiny urchin with one great staring eye, bouncing slowly
about its den while blows glance off its spines. It hates a certain
kind of sound: in the old tales the recorder's song makes it shrink
and split into smaller, faster urchins a blade can reach. Here it is
simply a long, hard fight against a hide like a pincushion. Guardian
of the Lizard, it leaves a heart container behind.

6.long: Gohma, a giant crab with one great eye, scuttles side to side.
6.description:
A huge, armoured, crablike monster with great pincers and a single
enormous eye set in its shell. Gohma scuttles back and forth along
the north side of its nest and spits fireballs. Blades and spells
can wear it down, but its eye snaps shut against any finishing blow
that is not an arrow: carry a bow, or the Silver Arrow, to end it.
Guardian of the Dragon, it leaves a heart container behind.

7.long: An ancient Aquamentus, scarred and horned, guards the Demon's lair.
7.description:
An older, larger Aquamentus, its green scales gone dark and its horn
chipped by a hundred battles. Like its young kin it paces a ledge at
the end of its hall and spits three fireballs at a time in a
spreading fan, but its hide is tougher and its fire hotter. Only its
horned head can be wounded. Guardian of the Demon, it bars the way
to the seventh shard of wisdom and leaves a heart container behind.

8.long: An ashen Gleeok, four heads swaying, fills the lair with flame.
8.description:
A colossal dragon with four long necks, its scales gone grey as ash
from centuries of its own fire. The ashen Gleeok stays fixed to the
north wall while four horned heads strike and spit fireballs in every
direction. Each head can be hacked free, and each one that falls
flies loose about the chamber, still spitting flame. Only when all
four are severed does the beast die. Guardian of the Lion, it keeps
the last shard of wisdom and leaves a heart container behind.

9.long: Ganon, the Prince of Darkness, lurks unseen in the dark.
9.description:
A towering, boarlike demon with blue hide, tusks and a black trident:
Ganon, the Prince of Darkness, bearer of the Triforce of Power. He
blinks out of sight and reappears elsewhere in the dark, hurling
fireballs at whoever stands against him, and any wound he is left
alone with closes. At his hip hangs a sword that was never his: the
Master Sword, taken from the hero's grave. Ordinary weapons can wound
him but never kill him. Beaten down, he collapses flashing red, and a
level 54+ hero must wield the Silver Arrow and SHOOT GANON to end it.
